/nl/course/2026/CMVB26KEUOX.content:
Hoe ontwerp je een ervaring in Virtual Reality, Augmented Reality of 360
­
graden video? Oftewel in XR!
🤟
Bij dit studieonderdeel leer je de ontwerp
­
en interactieprincipes die je hebt leren gebruiken in je studie toe nu toe, toe te passen en te adapteren in een virtuele interactieve omgeving in 3D. Je ontwerpt dus een ‘experience’ waarbij je van AR, VR en/of 360
­
-graden video gebruik maakt. Daarbij bepaal je voor je jezelf een relevante context voor je ontwerp. Anders gezegd, je werkt aan een ‘exploratief’ concept, je werkt niet aan een probleem voor een opdrachtgever, maar een ‘mogelijk’ probleem in een ‘mogelijke’ context. Voorwaarden zijn dat de ervaring educatief is en/of als zgn. ‘empathy tool’ (kruip in de huid van) ingezet kan worden. Het is uitdrukkelijk de bedoeling om jezelf uit te dagen de mogelijkheden van het medium te ontdekken en verkennen.
Opdracht
Je werkt in duo aan een eigen opdracht voor een XR-ervaring. Het proces en werk wordt ‘gebundeld’ in een individueel, visueel verslag. Daarin wordt het werk dat is gepresenteerd in een logische volgorde gezet en van achtergrond voorzien. De feedback die tijdens de presentatiebijeenkomsten is verzameld krijgt een duidelijke plek in het verslag als startpunt voor de ontwerpiteraties. Daarnaast toon je via een videolink de XR-ervaring zelf.

/nl/course/2026/CMVB18STG.outcomes:
Je werkt aan verschillende CMD-competenties en bijbehorende leeruitkomsten. De leeruitkomsten die horen bij de competenties EFGHI zijn verplicht. Je kiest zelf nog twee leeruitkomsten behorende bij de ABCD-competenties.
Leeruitkomsten waar je zelf twee uit mag kiezen, passend bij je stage (ABCD)
A) Je brengt de gebruikerscontext in kaart tijdens het ontwerpproces van de multimedia-producten die je ontwerpt tijdens de stage. Daarbij betrek je de eindgebruikers en andere stakeholders tijdens het proces.
B) Je vertaalt de wensen van de eindgebruiker en andere stakeholders in creatieve concepten voor (interactieve) multimedia producten en verantwoordt daarbij de gemaakte keuzes.
C) Je werkt voor de stageorganisatie verschillende concepten uit tot interactieve prototypes en (deel)producten. Daarbij gebruik je jouw kennis van interactie, storytelling, beleving, gedragsverandering en vormgeving van multimedia interfaces.
C) Je houdt bij het ontwerp en realiseren van jouw (interactieve) multimedia producten rekening met het draagvlak en de latere ingebruikname door de organisatie en verantwoordt daarbij de gemaakte keuzes.
D) Je valideert en verfijnt het ontwerp van de producten waar je tijdens de stage aan werkt. Dit doe je door de gebruiksvriendelijkheid en de kwaliteit van de gebruikerservaring te evalueren met de gebruikers door middel van verschillende evaluatiemethoden en
­
technieken.
Verplichte leeruitkomsten (EFGHI)
E) Je doorloopt het onderzoeksproces tijdens de stage op een methodische en navolgbare manier waarbij je een verantwoorde keuze maakt uit een breed palet aan onderzoeksmethoden en technieken die je inzet voor een beter ontwerp.
F) Je laat zien dat je zelfstandig je werkzaamheden kunt plannen, uitvoeren, monitoren en beheren.
G) Je laat zien dat je in teamverband binnen de stageorganisatie verschillende rollen en disciplines met elkaar kunt verbinden en hulp van experts inschakelt waar dat nodig is.
H) Je reflecteert op jouw leerproces en je visie op het werkveld aan de hand van je werkzaamheden tijdens je stageperiode. Dit laat je zien in een persoonlijk ontwikkelingsportfolio.
I)
Je laat zien een ondernemende en proactieve houding te hebben waarmee je kansen voor de stageorganisatie kan identificeren en creatieve innovatieve ideeën kan vertalen naar haalbare marktconcepten.
/nl/course/2026/CMVB18STG.content:
De stage is een externe leersituatie waarin je werkt aan de CMD
­
competenties (domeincompetenties en de professionele competenties). Dit doe je binnen de context van een professionele organisatie en onder begeleiding van een ervaren CMD professional. Tijdens de stage participeer je in de dagelijkse gang van zaken van de stageorganisatie. Je gaat hierbij:
•
CMD vaardigheden en kennis verbreden en verdiepen
•
Leren om deze kennis en vaardigheden in de praktijk toe te passen
•
Leren hoe een professionele organisatie werkt
•
Leren om doelen te stellen, hierop te reflecteren en jezelf te ontwikkelen.
De duur van de stage bedraagt 100 werkdagen (inclusief Stage Event: stageterugkomdag). Het uitgangspunt is een volledige werkweek op basis van de cao van de stageorganisatie.
Opdracht
Tijdens de stage werk je aan diverse opdrachten die gezamenlijk het portfolio vormen. Als bewijsmateriaal voor de verschillende competenties voeg je producten toe waaraan je tijdens de stage hebt gewerkt. Aan het einde van de stage wordt een eindgesprek gevoerd. Hierbij zijn de stagedocent en de stagebegeleider aanwezig. Halverwege de stage is er een verplicht StageEvent waar je aan andere studenten voorlichting/informatie geeft over je stage.

/nl/course/2026/CMVB20FUD.outcomes:
A. ORIËNTEREN EN BEGRIJPEN
Je kunt de context van het probleem, de wens van de gebruiker, doelstelling van de opdrachtgever, de belangen van belanghebbenden en de mogelijkheden van de technologie in kaart brengen en begrijpen.
• Het ontwerpvraagstuk (probleem/kans) en de doelstelling zijn helder afgebakend. De kernbegrippen en/of onderzoeksvragen zijn relevant voor het ontwerpvraagstuk en zijn richtinggevend voor het ontwerponderzoek.
• De student toont inzicht in de verschillende aspecten die relevant zijn voor het ontwerpvraagstuk. Inzichten zijn verkregen vanuit de opdrachtgever, de gebruikers en minimaal één ander perspectief (bijv. vanuit literatuur, best practices, experts).
• De student geeft blijk van een open en kritische houding en is in staat tot perspectiefwisseling.
B. VERBEELDEN EN CONCEPTUALISEREN
Je bedenkt ideeën en ontwikkelt concepten voor (interactieve) producten, diensten, en belevingen. Daarbij gaat het om het vinden van nieuwe wegen om tegemoet te komen aan de wensen van gebruikers, de doelstellingen van de opdrachtgever en aan andere belangen.
• De student ontwikkelt concepten voor producten, diensten en belevingen.
• De student is een creatieve denker, die kan divergeren en convergeren.
• De student toont daarnaast vindingrijkheid en resultaatgerichtheid.
• De student durft te experimenteren met (nieuwe) technologie(ën).
C. UITWERKEN EN PROTOTYPEREN
Je bent in staat om concepten vorm te geven en te concretiseren in prototypes. Je kunt je ontwerp inpassen in geldende standaarden en het productportfolio van het bedrijf.
• De student realiseert een digitaal interactief prototype, dat een passende representatie en simulatie vormt van het toekomstige digitale interactieve product.
• De student demonstreert beheersing van interactie-ontwerp en vormgeving (usability, user experience en andere relevante aspecten).
• De student laat zien dat het prototype tot stand gebracht is door middel van meerdere iteraties, via schetsen en/of wireframes en prototypes.
• De student onderbouwt de gekozen tools en technieken.
• De student durft te experimenteren met (nieuwe) tools en technieken.
D. EVALUEREN
Je bent in staat resultaten, die tijdens verschillende stadia van het ontwerpproces ontstaan, herhaaldelijk te toetsen op hun waarde en belang voor de wensen van de gebruiker/opdrachtgever.
• De student evalueert meermaals tussentijdse ontwerpen (bijv. concepten, wireframes, prototypes) en het uiteindelijke prototype. Daarbij voert de student minimaal eenmaal een gedegen, uitgebreider evaluatie uit.
• De student toont inzicht in de bruikbaarheid, betrouwbaarheid en validiteit van verkregen resultaten.
H. PERSOONLIJK EN GEËNGAGEERD ONTWERPEN
Je werkt vanuit een persoonlijke betrokkenheid bij de samenleving en vanuit een drive om deze te verbeteren. Je weet waar je staat en hoe je je kunt ontwikkelen.
• De student toont betrokkenheid bij maatschappelijke vraagstukken en streeft ernaar om impactvolle ontwerpoplossingen te creëren. De student heeft oog voor duurzaamheid, inclusiviteit en sociale verantwoordelijkheid in het eigen
/nl/course/2026/CMVB20FUD.content:
Het werkveld en de toepassingen van CMD veranderen snel. Het is belangrijk om de ontwikkelingen te blijven volgen om je een voorstelling te kunnen maken hoe toekomstige CMD technologie een rol gaat spelen bij toekomstige problemen. Future Design heeft tot doel om je ‘Futures Literacy’ te vergroten. Daarnaast leer je hoe je met je vaardigheden de (nabije) toekomst kunt vormgeven en hoe je als ontwerper kunt bijdragen aan toekomstige transities. Je wordt uitgedaagd om ontwerpen te maken die een beeld geven hoe toekomstige gebruikers technologie gebruiken om problemen op te lossen. Dat doe je binnen een zelfafgebakende probleemcontext, waarvan je zelf de relevantie onderbouwt.
Opdracht
Als duo maken jullie een ontwerp waarin wordt uitgewerkt hoe je met ‘toekomstige’ technieken problemen en uitdagingen kan oplossen. Elk duo levert twee prototypes op, die worden gepresenteerd tijdens een event of demo.
•  Prototype ‘Experience design’: een verbeelding van de beoogde ervaring van de gebruiker binnen een duidelijk afgebakende (toekomstige) probleemcontext.
•  Prototype ‘Proof of concept’: een gedeelte van de experience wordt uitgewerkt als werkend prototype.
•  Tot slot lever je individueel een ontwerpverslag waarmee je je ontwerpproces onderbouwt. Dit verslag maakt gebruik van de 'piramide-structuur', waarmee het op het afstuderen voorbereidt.

/nl/course/2026/CMVB20IWP.outcomes:
E)
De student maakt individueel gebruik van een gevarieerde verzameling van methoden en toont  voldoende inzet in de verschillende ontwerpfasen; exploratie, conceptontwikkeling, prototyping en evaluatie. De student komt via een proces van kritische afweging tot innovatieve concepten en een innovatief, interactief product dat aansluit op de design challenge.
F)
De student neemt verantwoordelijkheid en initiatief voor eigen proces en aandeel in het gezamenlijke resultaat en blijft actief betrokken na tegenslagen. De student richt zich hierbij ook individueel op het plannen van tijd en ureninzet. De student presenteert de onderbouwing, het proces en het digitaal interactieve product.
G)
De student werkt proactief (interdisciplinair) samen met mensen uit onderwijs, werkveld en onderzoek, concretiseert deze samenwerkingsrelatie om de opdracht zo goed mogelijk uit te voeren en organiseert eigen en andermans inbreng.
H) De student werkt actief aan zijn/haar professionele ontwikkeling en stelt persoonlijke leerdoelen op in relatie tot de opdracht van het Innovatieproject, en reflecteert op eigen ontwikkeling en nuanceert eigen perspectief met andermans inzichten.
/nl/course/2026/CMVB20IWP.content:
In dit project werk je met een ontwerpvraag of kans in een complexe, innovatieve technologische omgeving. Het ontwerpproces kenmerkt zich door ontwerpend onderzoek waarbij via meerdere iteraties een innovatief, onderbouwd prototype of ecosysteem wordt opgeleverd. Bij dit proces zijn een aantal fasen te onderscheiden die complementair zijn en elkaar in verschillende ritmes kunnen opvolgen; Begrijpen, Observeren, Definiëren, Ideeën ontwikkelen, Prototype maken, Testen en Reflecteren.
Je werkt samen met andere studenten, onderzoekers en organisaties uit de praktijk. Via coaching ligt de nadruk op je eigen leervragen en initiatief. Je maakt kennis met nieuwe werkvelden en leert verschillende rollen en belangen begrijpen.
Je wordt aangemoedigd om:
Verantwoordelijkheid te nemen voor je eigen leerproces.
Actief te communiceren met coaches en opdrachtgevers.
Een professionele, onderzoekende en ondernemende houding te ontwikkelen.
Multidisciplinair en maatschappelijk bewust te werken.
Innovatieve ontwerpprocessen te initiëren waarbij je relevante stakeholders betrekt.
Het project loopt over twee periodes met twee feedbackmomenten en een eindbeoordeling in periode 2. De totale studiebelasting is 10 EC.
Opdracht
Je gaat aan de slag met een complexe ontwerpvraag voor een praktijkpartner. Het doel is een innovatief ecosysteem met digitale interactieve producten te ontwerpen dat een bewezen meerwaarde heeft voor de beoogde gebruiker en context.

/nl/course/2026/CMVB23HUT.outcomes:
A: Je doet literatuuronderzoek naar manieren waarop technologie kan worden ontworpen en gebruikt om de menselijke ervaring te verbeteren en doet onderzoek naar de ervaring/beleving die de applicatie of installatie heeft op gebruikers (doelgroep).
Je formuleert op grond van deze onderzoeken de kerninteracties in de vorm van design requirements en formuleert toevoegingen op deze design requirements waardoor de ervaring zou kunnen worden verbeterd.
B. Je genereert ideeën/concepten door het toepassen van verschillende creatieve methoden op basis van de geformuleerde (nieuwe) design requirements. Deze concepten weeg je af tegen de geformuleerde design requirements en maakt op grond hiervan een afgewogen keuze voor een definitief concept dat bestaat uit een toevoeging of herdesign van de onderzochte applicatie/installatie.
C. Je past verschillende methoden en technieken toe voor het realiseren van het prototype. Je laat dat zien aan de hand van hi-fi visualisaties van een hi-fi prototype.
D: Je analyseert een bestaande applicatie of installatie op de kerninteracties en de effecten die dat op de (gebruikers)ervaring heeft.
/nl/course/2026/CMVB23HUT.content:
De cursus Human-Technology Interaction is ontworpen om jou een diepgaand inzicht te bieden in de manier waarop technologie kan worden ontworpen en gebruikt om de menselijke ervaring te verbeteren. De course omvat een breed scala aan onderwerpen, variërend van menselijke cognitie en emotionele reacties tot ergonomie en interface-ontwerp.
De cursus geeft een overzicht van de menselijke cognitie en hoe deze ons vermogen om te begrijpen en te communiceren beïnvloedt.
Je leert over verschillende cognitieve processen, zoals perceptie, geheugen en aandacht, en hoe deze kunnen worden toegepast bij het ontwerpen van gebruikersinterfaces, installaties en (kern)interacties met deze digitale technologieën. Denk hierbij aan interacties met "eenvoudige" web/ mobile applicaties tot aan interacties met  "complexe installaties" die je tegenwoordig meer en meer in musea of openbare gebouwen aantreft.
De opgedane kennis pas je toe in een eigen (her)ontwerp van de belangrijkste interacties van een interface of installatie. Je verwerkt hierbij de eerder verkregen inzichten over hoe emoties ons gedrag en besluitvorming beïnvloeden en hoe technologie kan worden ontworpen om deze emoties te ondersteunen of te beïnvloeden.
De cursus omvat praktische projecten en casestudy's waarbij studenten de kans krijgen om de theorie in de praktijk toe te passen en hun vaardigheden te ontwikkelen op het gebied van ontwerpen voor de menselijke ervaring.

/nl/course/2026/CMVB23PPT.outcomes:
B) Je analyseert design requirements en vertaalt deze naar concrete kwaliteitseisen voor een product.
B) Je past het prototype aan op basis van evaluatieresultaten, waarbij je gebruik maakt van geschikte evaluatiemethoden.
C) Je creëert een prototype van een digitaal product dat voldoet aan de gestelde kwaliteitseisen.
C) Je selecteert en gebruikt geschikte tools en technieken voor de ontwikkeling van het prototype, deze onderbouw je met een heldere argumentatie.
D) Je beoordeelt je eigen prototype systematisch op kwaliteit, bruikbaarheid en toegankelijkheid, met een onderbouwde keuze voor de evaluatiemethode.
D) Je evalueert prototypes van anderen op kwaliteit, bruikbaarheid en toegankelijkheid, en communiceert de bevindingen constructief.
/nl/course/2026/CMVB23PPT.content:
Product Prototyping is een verdiepend vak waarbij studenten leren om kwalitatief hoogwaardige prototypes te ontwikkelen. De focus van dit vak ligt daarbij op vakmanschap en de kwaliteit van producten die ontwikkeld worden. Studenten kiezen zelf aan wat voor soort product ze willen werken en kunnen zo hun eigen verdieping binnen de opleiding zoeken.
In dit vak leer je hoe je de belangrijkste ontwerp voorwaarden kan distilleren en hoe deze vervolgens vertaald kunnen worden naar een bruikbaar product voor de eindgebruiker. Je leert bij het ontwikkelen van prototypes de juiste tools en technieken te gebruiken die passend zijn voor het product wat je wilt realiseren. De student wordt daarbij ondersteund met workshops door docenten met verschillende specialismen. Tijdens het ontwerpproces leer je hoe je prototypes op een professionele manier kan evalueren door feedback van elkaar en experts te verzamelen.
Opdracht
Voor dit vak maak je op individuele basis een interactief prototype van een digitaal product naar keuze. Tijdens het ontwerpproces evalueer je het prototype op regelmatige basis om zo verschillende iteraties te kunnen maken. De kwaliteitseisen, ontwerpkeuzes en evaluaties beschrijf je in een ontwerpprocesverslag.

/nl/course/2026/CMVB24AFS.content:
Tijdens het afstuderen laat je zien dat je alle competenties van CMD op eindniveau beheerst. Daarom doorloop je de ontwerpcyclus zoals gebruikelijk en itereer je van een probleem (of kans of vraagstuk) tot en met een geëvalueerd prototype. Je maakt een afstudeerportfolio dat bestaat uit verschillende onderdelen zoals een prototype, een ontwerpverslag, de bewijzen uit de verschillende fasen van de ontwerpcyclus en een reflectieverslag (zie de afstudeerhandleiding voor een volledig overzicht van de portfolio-onderdelen).
Je kunt alleen afstuderen op basis van een afstudeeropdracht die is goedgekeurd door de afstudeercoördinator of beoordelingscommissie afstuderen (BCA). Je wordt begeleid bij het zoeken naar die opdracht en het opstellen van het aanvraagformulier. Dit gebeurt tijdens de Introductieweek Jaar 4 (start van het eerste semester of tweede semester bij februari instroom), de Bootcamp Afstuderen (tijdens periode 1 of periode 3 (februari instroom)) en de Kick Start Afstuderen (eerste week van het afstudeersemester). Tijdens de Kick Start Afstuderen maak je een stappenplan met een tijdsplanning.
Tijdens je afstuderen word je begeleid door je afstudeerbegeleider en krijg je op basis van afspraken gestructureerde feedback. De afstudeerbegeleider krijg je toegewezen door de afstudeercoördinator.
Opdracht
Je ontwerpt en ontwikkelt een interactieve media-ervaring waarbij je je ontwerpproces onderbouwt in een portfolio. Hiermee toon je aan dat je de eindcompetenties van CMD beheerst. De opdracht zoek je zelf in het werkveld, rekening houdend met de criteria uit de afstudeerhandleiding.
Je kiest zelf het logische startpunt in de ontwerpcyclus: begin je met een probleem, een bestaand product of prototype, of start je met een eerste prototype om verder te itereren? Tijdens het eindgesprek (examen) demonstreer je je uiteindelijke ontwerp en proces aan de hand van het portfolio en prototype.

/nl/course/2026/GTVP21PDP.content:
In Project Design and Prototyping, students will work in teams to solve a real design challenge, to create a mixed-media tabletop game that will be played during the following year's CMGT Introduction Week by the incoming first-year students.
In solving the design brief, student teams are supported by project coaches, and a series of workshops and learning streams, including Intercultural Competence; Game Design Tools; 2D Visual Design; and an introduction to working with digital technology, Play with Tech.
Students are expected to put in the necessary hours and effort to complete a working, iterated prototype of their game, and to have tested their game with fellow students.
The course is assessed by a demonstration, in which the working prototype is shown to teachers and fellow students; and by a development portfolio, assembled over the length of the course, in which the student provides evidence of what they have done and what they have learned.

/nl/course/2026/GTVP21FUP.content:
In Futureproof, students will focus on what it means to be a creator of new technologies, asking themselves who they are and who they wish to become. Who are games for? What kind of people make them? They will learn the necessary skills in writing, presenting, and student behaviour to form a baseline of communication, orienting them on what is expected of a CMGT student.
The student will write an individual text where they reflect on their own future role in the industry. What and who inspired them to choose a career in this industry? How do they see their future?
The student will also work with others to give a presentation and will reach out to someone in the industry to help inform them. They will then work together to create an engaging and informative presentation.

/nl/course/2026/GTVP21P2D.content:
Content
In Project 2D Game Development, students will work in teams to create a digital game solution that will be played during the following year's CMGT Introduction Week by the incoming first-year students.
Student teams will work following the Agile Scrum method to develop a working digital game prototype in GameMaker. Building on the intercultural communicative competence (ICC) that still takes centre stage, the student will consider accessibility and inclusivity (Ethics) when making design choices for their digital game.
Design Constraints
The game must be digital.
The game must be made in GameMaker.
The game must be freestanding and playable during Introduction Week the following year.
In solving this design brief, student teams are supported by project coaches and a series of workshops and learning streams, including Design Ethics, 2D Programming, 2D Art Tools, and Agile SCRUM.
Students are expected to put in the necessary hours and effort to complete a working, iterated prototype of their game and to have tested their prototype with fellow students and experts.
Assessment
The course is assessed by a demonstration, where the prototype is shown to and playable by teachers and students; by a development portfolio, assembled over the duration of the course, in which the student provides evidence of what they have done and what they have learned; and a Criterium Based Interview (CBI) where students are interviewed about the contents of the development portfolio.

/nl/course/2026/GTVP21PPF.content:
Conten
t
Playful Pasts and Futures is a course that historicises games and confronts students with the questions like “Why do we study games?”. Students will learn how play is a form of learning and how we use games to explore the possibilities of new technology. The course touches on the history of the internet, technology and games and the ethics connected to it.
Essential to understanding interactive systems and their possibilities is to be able to see the elements of which a system consists and how they relate to the experience the system intends to deliver. For budding new technologies these elements might be clear, but the experiences they could deliver are still being explored. A fundamental part of exploring these experiences is to find goals and interactions for new technology that stimulates familiarization and sparks engaging interaction.
By being able to assess and identify the core tenets of interactive systems, the student is challenged to reassess their own relation to the interactive systems they know. In turn, this understanding opens the student up for identifying new interactions or applying old interactions in novel ways; and enables the student to assess the current interactive digital media industries and identify new opportunities to act on. The course is assessed by a poster presentation and a written report.

/nl/course/2026/GTVP24PPP.content:
“Making a game in a team to develop yourself!”
In Project 3D Prototyping and Production, students will concept, develop, and produce a digital game as a solution to a chosen design challenge. Students will use evaluation and 3D game development tools to create a finished 3D solution to their design challenge. The finished solution will be evaluated with the target audience to ensure it meets the initial project brief and will be iterated upon, based on the findings of the evaluations.
Design Brief
Games and playful design can be used to address real social challenges, from small scale ('how to get more people to use this service?') to large scale (‘how to change people's behaviour around water usage?’) and everything in between. The theme for this block revolves around three 'Spaces': nature spaces, public spaces, and cultural spaces. The student will create, develop, and evaluate a 3D entertainment game to address one of the cases around these spaces.
Design Constraints
the game must be made using 3D tools (think Unity, Blender)
the game concept must address the project briefing.
the game concept must be evaluated with the users of the given space (think Research).
the game must exist in finished prototype form, suitable to be deployed in the relevant channel.
In solving the design brief, student teams are supported by project coaches, and a series of workshops and learning streams, including 3D Creative Media; 3D Game Programming; Game Design Tools; and Research.
Students are expected to put in the necessary hours in ideation and effort to have a tested, iterated, and finished prototype of their game, and to have tested their game with both fellow students and end-users.
Assessment
The course is assessed via a demonstration, in which the working prototype is shown to teachers and fellow students; by a development portfolio, assembled over the duration of the course, in which the student provides evidence of what they have done and what they have learned; and a Criterium Based Interview (CBI) were students are interviewed about the contents of the development portfolio.

/nl/course/2026/GTVP21VOU.content:
The student will be offered several cases of products that can benefit from an improved user interface and user experience. They select one case to focus on and analyse the current UI and UX. During workshops general principles of UI and UX will be discussed. Students will work with methods (tools) of front-end prototyping that enable them to redesign the product of their case based on their just acquired insights.
UI and UX principles will be offered in the slides and by referencing general available sources online. As a book on UX design, human factors, and usability the book ‘The Gamer’s Brain’, by Celia Hodent will be used. This book is written for multimedia professionals in the creative media and game technology industry to better understand what UX is, its importance, how to improve games (or other multimedia products), and in what way UX can be integrated in in their production pipeline in different phases of production.
The workshops on UI design will use an industry standard prototyping tool. The student will learn to create low-fidelity prototypes to test new setups and how to iterate on them towards a high-fidelity prototype for testing more fleshed-out ideas. Having developed a high-fidelity prototype, students will conduct a short evaluation to find out whether their redesign has achieved its design goal. As a closure for the course the student will digitally hand in their prototypes and a report outlining their design rationale.

/nl/course/2026/GTVP21FUS.content:
This course functions as a 'mirror capstone' of Year 1. Students will create a showcase portfolio to present themselves to the industry by identifying appropriate channels, their best work (so far), unique value and core qualities. Additionally, they will develop the skill to pitch their value in a concise format. The target audience is the Company Supervisor (Instructor) of their desired Internship Company.
The course is assessed via a hand-in of a showcase portfolio and a pitch presentation.

/nl/course/2026/GTVB22NTE.content:
Students will work in groups to create a game using a chosen technology from a selection provided. Students will explore that technology through the development of their game, uncovering the ethical, technical and artistic limits of their chosen technology. Building on Playful Pasts and Futures in Year 1, students will use games as a tool to map the contours and possibilities of their chosen technology, discovering and creating new uses for their technology. Students will engage with game engines, 3D modelling tools, theories of technology and ethical questions in their project.
Students work individually to create a development portfolio in which they submit evidence of their attainment of the competencies of the course, using as evidence the work they have done during the time of the project, including process, prototype and work done outside the project.
Design Brief  One of the main uses of games is as a tool to explore the possible uses of new technologies. In this course, students are challenged to make a game for 30 years in the future: what will that game look like, how will it play, who will play it? What is the next hit game for VR? What is the next technology to be mainstream in gaming? In attempting to address this design brief, students will address the question of ‘what is a game’ and will attempt to position themselves in this future.
Design Constraints
• The game must be made in Unity.
• The game must use one of the selected technologies.
• The game must have a visual style appropriate to the technology.
• The game must be playable at the demonstration.
• The game cannot have shooting.
In solving the design brief, student teams are supported by project coaches, and a series of workshops related to VR Development and Futures Literacy;
Students are expected to put in the necessary hours and effort to have a tested concept and a working prototype of their game.
The course is assessed via a demonstration, in which the working prototype is shown to teachers and fellow students; and by a development portfolio, assembled over the duration of the course, in which the student provides evidence of what they have done and what they have learned.
The entry requirement to this project is having passed GTVP24PPP in the CMGT first year programme.

/nl/course/2026/GTVB22NTA.content:
In New Technology Adaptation, students will work in teams to build a solution to specific problem of a real client using mobile technology. Students will work following an Agile process to develop, iterate and test a solution to the client’s design brief. In making their solutions, students will address the extent to which the solution meets the needs of the target audience and the appropriateness of the technological solution.
Design Brief
The design brief for the assignment will be provided by the client.
Design Constraints
• The solution must be made in the technology preferred by the client.
• Feedback on the proposed solution must be gathered from the client prior to the final demonstration.
• The solution must be justified based on appropriate user experience research and must be playable at the demonstration.
• The visual style must be appropriate to the needs of the target audience.
In solving the design brief, student teams are supported by project coaches, and a series of workshops related to Mobile Development and UX.
Students are expected to put in the necessary hours and effort to have a tested concept and a working prototype of their game, and to have tested their game with the target audience.
The course is assessed via a demonstration, in which the working prototype is shown to teachers and fellow students; and by a development portfolio, assembled over the duration of the course, in which the student provides evidence of what they have done and what they have learned.
The entry requirement to this project is having passed GTVP24PPP in the CMGT first year programme

The students will be provided a bare-bones game template that students will expand upon. They will add extra assets, extra mechanics or both. They are free to work in groups if they choose to do so. The template is a simple game setup with straightforward code and assets.
The student will be assessed individually but is allowed to work in groups.

/nl/course/2026/GTVB22GL.content:
During Gamelab, you will form start-up groups and work in partnership with fellow students and professionals to build a concept, pitch your solution and develop it in order to convince the judges of its potential. The goal of GameLab is that you have a product that can be published on one of the major platforms upon completion (eg, Steam, AppStore, Itch.io, etc)
In a series of workshops, coaching sessions and presentations you will proceed through a series of gates in which your concept and business case will be assessed by professionals. During the course of the project the professionals will have the ability to not accept various ideas as potential products. This means only the best ideas get to progress to the point of publishing.
You will develop according to the latest software engineering methods using production specifications determined by your team, the experts and coaches. By critically assessing your budget, role requirements, technology and concept you will guide your development team towards the release of your product.
As a professional individual you will provide your team the needed hours and effort to complete the development of the products. This means in most cases you will put in lots of hours to develop the needed assets and code.
During this course you will receive coaching from professionals on art, design, audience research, user experience and development. But it is your task to ensure you have access to the required information to succeed.
In a final demonstration to the judges and fellow students you will show the potential of your product. This includes the actual working product, but also an insight on your production process. You will provide evidence of and reflection on the work you have done in a development portfolio, and will defend that portfolio in an individual competency based interview.
The course is assessed via a demonstration, in which the working prototype is shown to teachers and fellow students; and by a development portfolio, assembled over the duration of the course, in which the student provides evidence of what they have done and what they have learned.
The entry requirement to this project is having passed GTVP24PPP in the CMGT first year programme.

The students will present the incremental stages of their work and discuss crucial decisions made during the creation of their game-ready animated character within a real-time render scene.
The real-time render scene showcases the character's personality through the utilization of thorough research, references, 3d modelling, rigging, animation, and visualization techniques. The digital, interactive, real-time scene in the game engine enables the player to activate various animations.

This course will help you to develop your skills as a game professional, focusing on game design tools and level design and development. There will be an individual assignment using theories, tools, and skills used in the work field, to relay your knowledge and skills of level design into a working prototype.
As a designer you will come up with an innovative and creative game concept that will show off your skills as a future professional. In a written game design document you will showcase your design with a focus on level design. You will then develop a level of your game in an industry tool to showcase your skills.
The student will be able to come up with a game concept and translate this into a prototype of a level design while thinking about how the elements of level design work together.

Students can choose anything from the aforementioned products, as long as they submit a proposal that meets preset requirements (using UE4/UE5 is one of them). /nl/course/2026/GTVB24ELAN.content:
For this elective, students will focus on creating a portfolio ready animation(s). These could have any kind of application ranging from, but not limited to: short films, music videos, advertisements or an animated website.
Go wild and use the LED screen in the Spacelab to record a video doing a dance off against your own animated avatar! Use your work from Narrative Design and bring your story world to life! Take your creature from Creature Design and animate it for a gripping cutscene.
The goal for students is to comprehend the principles of animation such as sense of weight, timing and style, how to apply them to their chosen concept and explore animation techniques (eg, 2D, 3D, Claymation etc) used in different industries.
By completing practical exercises in class like creating small animations, students build up the foundation to make their concept come to life. Additionally, they’ll be collecting supporting material for their design process on a week-by-week basis.
Students will then storyboard and plan their workflow, determining the appropriate techniques and technologies required to create a portfolio worthy piece.
Students are free to experiment, think outside of the box and pursue a topic and technique they are passionate about. This freedom extends both to the nature of the project
and the
makeup of the creative team. Students can decide to work as an individual, in pairs or in a team. If more people work on a project, then more will be possible, yet more will be expected in terms of complexity and scope.
A proposal will be discussed to realistically match the timeframe and expected workload.
The final product will be a rendered animation that is expected to have a coherent concept, theme, style and purpose.

You will define your industry focus and expectations whether in product design, game apparel, animation, or other fashion-adjacent industries. Throughout the elective, you will develop a small fashion collection presented through digital 3D renders
You will learn fashion industry design and research methods that integrate physical and digital experimentation, enabling you to set and achieve self-defined standards. The final submission will consist of a design book that includes your research, workflow, and completed renders.

/nl/course/2026/GTVB22ELAI.content:
The field of AI is evolving rapidly, while simultaneously revolutionizing the field of Creative Media & Game Technology. New developments such as art and level generation, deep reinforcement learning for automatic AI behavior training, and automatic upscaling of old textures have large impacts on the industry.
You will need to research, understand, apply and expand these technologies, in order to show you can adapt to any new technologies that might come your way in the near or far future.
Over the course of this elective, we will address various topics from classical AI technologies such as search trees and state machines to modern AI technologies such as neural networks and large language models. The explanations of the functionality 'under the hood' helps demystify the often black box nature of AI systems.
For this course we expect at least some familiarity with programming, in order for you to develop your own prototype. There is no programming language/framework requirement.

/nl/course/2026/GTVB22ELSG.content:
With a growing interest in the world for "Games to Grow", "Edugames" and other initiatives, the field of Serious Gaming is growing, and there is a need for well-thought-out games which teach technical and critical thinking skills developed by professionals. This Elective will dive into how "Learning Mechanics" translate to "Game Mechanics" and how games can be designed and facilitated with the purpose of solving local problems for a student-defined audience.
By experiencing and analyzing various Serious Games, students will comprehend the effectiveness and utility of games as solutions for complex problems. Through research and testing, students will define a problem statement for a self-chosen target audience. They will then test a prototype to determine its effectiveness and analyze the results. To complete the serious game cycle, students will create a facilitation manual that accompanies their serious game.
Assignment
The student works on an assignment from a real-world client. They make a Serious Game Solution prototype and accompanying Facilitation Manual.
The Prototype needs to be based on research on and understanding of the target audience for the case. It also needs to be tested and experienced by the target audience and client as well as addressing the problem statement.
The Facilitation Manual follows the CMGT dresscode and is easy to comprehend. It needs to include the learning goals for the target audience and explains how the Serious Game Solution helps achieve those goals. The Facilitation Manual also has explanatory notes on the development of the game and explains how the game needs to be set up and played / experienced. It describes the roles and tasks of the facilitator before, during and after the Serious Game experience.
Objective:
The student will research, prototype, and test a serious game solution to a problem for a specific target audience. The student will write a Facilitation manual and prototype.
Description of the Assessment task
During the course, the student learns the process for designing a serious game solution to a self-chosen problem. The student conducts research into the problem, defines learning goals which are used to inform the design requirements of the Serious Game solution. The design requirements inform the game mechanics used in the serious game. The student hands in a Serious Game prototype and accompanying Facilitation Manual. In it, they explain how the prototype is run AND how to maximise results during the reflection exercise afterwards.
The student hands in a Serious Game Prototype and the accompanying Facilitation Manual through blackboard. This prototype can be either digital or physical. The Facilitation Manual needs to be delivered in PDF format.

Students will be challenged with examples of works with diverse storytelling, theme, interesting characters, plot conflicts, world-building, and other narrative design elements.

/nl/course/2026/GTVB23ELPA.content:
Procedural generation using algorithms is an effective way of using available computing power to create unique assets, levels, worlds or even universes. This elective focuses on teaching students about the different methods of procedural generation available, how to use these methods and how these methods can help in creating unique experiences.
The student will learn to set up their own use-case and implement specific learning goals. Starting with the exploration of the application and boundaries of a technique and the relevant software. First by replicating examples of procedural techniques and later applying different techniques in their own use-case. The solution to the use-case will be achieved by weighing the pros and cons of possible solutions and making the right design choices. These design choices are showcased in a presentation.
The student will build a product that consists of multiple procedural generation methodologies (noise, scatter, parametric etc). The specific product can be a scene that is procedurally generated or a tool that can be used to create new procedural created assets (city builder etc.). The assessment product will be a showreel video of the product suitable for the professional portfolio.

/nl/course/2026/GTVB23ELRO.content:
The Robotics elective is designed to provide students with an opportunity to explore the world of robotics and its applications. Through guided project work, students collaborate in teams to build robots that can express different emotions and interactions with users. Throughout the elective, students not only gain a solid foundation in the basics of electronics, Arduino programming, basic sensors, and automation in both software and hardware design but also in social interactions, empathy and how emotions can be detected and shown.
The first few weeks of the course focus on fundamental electronics and Arduino programming, while the latter weeks explore more advanced topics such as social interaction, empathy, and behaviour. Students are encouraged to take on specialized roles within their teams, while still learning the basics of electronics, power systems, basic sensors, Arduino programming, visual detection, and more.
Assessment of each student’s progress and understanding is based on a group report that describes the build process and outlines how each group member contributed to the final product. In addition, each student participates in an individual interview to assess their intrinsic understanding of the fundamental topics covered in the course. The minimum requirement for each student is to design and implement a functional contribution to the robot in each of the following areas: electronics, Arduino coding, and mechanical design/construction and how these can show and influence the state of the robot.
By the end of the course, students should be able to apply their newly acquired skills and knowledge to create a functional robot that can express different emotions and interact with users. Students who wish to pursue more advanced topics in robotics can continue their studies in machine learning, advanced AI, more advanced sensor systems, or industry-standard development platforms. The Robotics elective offers an exciting opportunity for students to develop their creativity, problem-solving skills, and critical thinking abilities, all while having fun building robots.

To test (parts of) a game, you need people to experience your ideas. In the Rapid Prototyping elective you will build the skills and confidence to quickly develop representative, playable prototypes. Prototypes that you can use to test out your ideas.
The best way to learn is to do, so you will be creating prototypes based on provided themes and from any perspective you want, be it artist, designer or programmer. For each prototype you have two weeks, so imagine the joy and excitement of a Game Jam but feeling less groggy!
The course is set up as such that there is a lot of opportunity to generate ideas and for feedback on what you have created. At the end, you pick your best of three prototypes and iterate upon it adding an additional, provided theme.

/nl/course/2026/GTVB23ELGA.content:
A mere few seconds of playing your preferred game without sound will make you appreciate how critical audio is in creating an engaging experience. This elective focuses on the production of sound effects, ambient audio and voice recording using a Digital Audio Workstation (DAW).
In this course, students will master audio manipulation by utilizing a DAW to implement audio theory, recording methods, microphones, sound effects, mixing, and integrating audio into a game engine. The assessment for this class is showcasing audio for a game or trailer, complete with sound effects, ambient audio, (looped) music and voice over, which demonstrates the practical application of the audio theory taught in this course.

What monetization models did or didn't work and why? What marketing strategies were or were not appropriate? Why not? Together, these elements of the pitch deck prepare the student for professionally pitching their game to a publisher.

/nl/course/2026/GTVB23ELSG2.content:
With a growing interest in the world for "Games to Grow", "Edugames" and other initiatives, the field of Serious Gaming is growing, and there is a need for well thought out games which teach technical and critical thinking skills developed by professionals. This Elective will dive into how "Learning Mechanics" translate to "Game Mechanics" and how games can be designed and facilitated with the purpose of solving local problems for a student-defined audience.
By experiencing and analyzing various Serious Games, students will comprehend the effectiveness and utility of games as solutions for complex problems. Through research and testing, students will define a problem statement for a self-chosen target audience. They will then test a prototype to determine its effectiveness and analyze the results. To complete the serious game cycle, students will create a facilitation manual that accompanies their serious game.
Assignment:
The student works on an assignment from a real-world client. They make a Serious Game Solution prototype and accompanying Facilitation Manual.
The Prototype needs to be based on research on and understanding of the target audience for the case. It also needs to be tested and experienced by the target audience and client as well as addressing the problem statement.
The Facilitation Manual follows the CMGT dresscode and is easy to comprehend. It needs to include the learning goals for the target audience and explains how the Serious Game Solution helps achieve those goals. The Facilitation Manual also has explanatory notes on the development of the game and explains how the game needs to be set up and played / experienced. It describes the roles and tasks of the facilitator before, during and after the Serious Game experience.
Objective:
The student will research, prototype, and test a serious game solution to a problem for a specific target audience.

/nl/course/2026/GTVB23ELUR2.outcomes: For this elective level 2 students have to write 5 personal learning outcomes ((LOL) that adapt to their level, development needs and the CMGT competencies. The learning outcomes have to be approved by the lecturer of the course.
/nl/course/2026/GTVB23ELUR2.content:
Choosing the Unreal elective a subsequent time requires you to formulate five of your own learning goals. The lecturers must approve your learning goals in order for you to be able to use them. You must base your learning goals on the CMGT competencies (on level 2) to create a digital product
The entry requirement for this elective is that the student has passed level 1 of the elective.

/nl/course/2026/GTVB23ELAI2.outcomes:
Learning Outcomes
For this elective level 2 students have to write 5 personal learning outcomes that adapt to their level, development needs and the CMGT LOLs. The learning outcomes have to be approved by the lecturer of the course.
/nl/course/2026/GTVB23ELAI2.content:
The field of AI is evolving rapidly, while simultaneously revolutionizing the field of Creative Media & Game Technology. New developments such as art and level generation, deep reinforcement learning for automatic AI behavior training, and automatic upscaling of old textures have large impacts on the industry.
You will need to research, understand, apply and expand these technologies, in order to show you can adapt to any new technologies that might come your way in the near or far future.
Over the course of this elective, we will address various topics from classical AI technologies such as search trees and state machines to modern AI technologies such as neural networks and large language models. The explanations of the functionality 'under the hood' helps demystify the often black box nature of AI systems.
For this course we expect at least some familiarity with programming, in order for you to develop your own prototype. There is no programming language/framework requirement.
The entry requirement for this elective is that the student has passed level 1 of the elective.

/nl/course/2026/GTVB26ELDF2.outcomes: For this elective level 2 students have to write 5 personal learning outcomes that adapt to their level, development needs and the CMGT competencies. The learning outcomes have to be approved by the lecturer of the course.
/nl/course/2026/GTVB26ELDF2.content:
During the fashion elective, you will challenge your creativity by bridging the gap between game technologies and the fashion industries. You will define your industry focus and expectations whether in product design, game apparel, animation, or other fashion-adjacent industries. Throughout the elective, you will develop a small fashion collection presented through digital 3D renders
You will learn fashion industry design and research methods that integrate physical and digital experimentation, enabling you to set and achieve self-defined standards. The final submission will consist of a design book that includes your research, workflow, and completed renders.

/nl/course/2026/GTVB23ELCD2.outcomes:
Learning Outcomes
For this elective level 2 students have to write 5 personal learning outcomes that adapt to their level, development needs and the CMGT competencies. The learning outcomes have to be approved by the lecturer of the course.
/nl/course/2026/GTVB23ELCD2.content:
Content
Students will be creating a game ready character or creature from concept to 3D model. The model will have to convince that the students thought about the “why”, by creating a backstory that matches the visual characteristics, for example, physical abilities, use of colour etc. Why does my creature/character have this shape or colour? If it is an Aquatic creature, how does this influence its looks, its skin, its movements etc. This elective go through all the steps starting with brainstorming, visual research, concept-art, followed by modelling/sculpting, retopology, textures and hair/fur.
The entry requirement for this elective is that the student has passed level 1 of the elective.

/nl/course/2026/GTVB24ELAN2.outcomes:
For this elective level 2 students have to write 5 personal learning outcomes that adapt to their level, development needs and the CMGT competencies.
These learning outcomes must be clearly different from level 1 learning outcomes in the judgement of the lecturer of the course and require the approval of the course coordinator.
/nl/course/2026/GTVB24ELAN2.content:
For this elective, students will focus on creating a portfolio ready animation(s). These could have any kind of application ranging from, but not limited to: short films, music videos, advertisements or an animated website.
Go wild and use the LED screen in the Spacelab to record a video doing a dance off against your own animated avatar! Use your work from Narrative Design and bring your story world to life! Take your creature from Creature Design and animate it for a gripping cutscene.
The goal for students is to comprehend the principles of animation such as sense of weight, timing and style, how to apply them to their chosen concept and explore animation techniques (eg, 2D, 3D, Claymation etc) used in different industries.
By completing practical exercises in class like creating small animations, students build up the foundation to make their concept come to life. Additionally, they’ll be collecting supporting material for their design process on a week-by-week basis.
Students will then storyboard and plan their workflow, determining the appropriate techniques and technologies required to create a portfolio worthy piece.
Students are free to experiment, think outside of the box and pursue a topic and technique they are passionate about. This freedom extends both to the nature of the project and the makeup of the creative team. Students can decide to work as an individual, in pairs or in a team. If more people work on a project, then more will be possible, yet more will be expected in terms of complexity and scope.
A proposal will be discussed to realistically match the timeframe and expected workload.
The final product will be a rendered animation that is expected to have a coherent concept, theme, style and purpose.
The entry requirement for this elective is that the student has passed level 1 of the elective.

/nl/course/2026/GTVB24ELGA2.outcomes:
Learning Outcomes
For this elective level 2 students have to write 5 personal learning outcomes that adapt to their level, development needs and the CMGT LOLs. The learning outcomes have to be approved by the lecturer of the course.
/nl/course/2026/GTVB24ELGA2.content:
Game Sound. A mere few seconds of playing your preferred game without sound will make you appreciate how critical audio is in creating an engaging experience. This elective focuses on the production of sound effects, ambient audio, music and voice recording using a Digital Audio Workstation (DAW).
In this course, students will master audio manipulation by utilizing a DAW to implement audio theory, recording methods, microphones, sound effects, mixing, and integrating audio into a game engine. The assessment  for this class is showcasing audio for a game or trailer, complete with sound effects, ambient audio, (looped) music and voice over, which demonstrates the practical application of the audio theory taught in this course.

/nl/course/2026/GTVB24ELMM2.outcomes: For this elective level 2 students have to write 5 personal learning outcomes that adapt to their level, development needs and the CMGT competencies. The learning outcomes have to be approved by the lecturer of the course.
/nl/course/2026/GTVB24ELMM2.content:
The goal of this assessment is for students to create an investor-ready pitch deck (with appendix), for a game they designed previously or are in the process of designing.
Pitch Deck: Your solution for monetizing and marketing your game
Appendix: The research you did, what you point to when an investor asks you a question.
What monetization models didn't work and why? What marketing strategies were not appropriate? Why not? Together, these elements of the pitch deck prepare the student for professionally pitching their game to a publisher.
The entry requirement for this elective is that the student has passed level 1 of the elective.

/nl/course/2026/GTVB24ELPA2.outcomes:
Learning Outcomes
For this elective level 2, students have to write 5 personal learning outcomes that adapt to their level, development needs and the CMGT LOLs. The learning outcomes have to be approved by the lecturer of the course.
/nl/course/2026/GTVB24ELPA2.content:
Procedural generation using algorithms is an effective way of using available computing power to create unique assets, levels, worlds or even universes. This elective focuses on teaching students about the different methods of procedural generation available, how to use these methods and how these methods can help in creating unique experiences.
The student will learn to set up their own use-case and implement specific learning goals. Starting with the exploration of the application and boundaries of a technique and the relevant software. First by replicating examples of procedural techniques and later applying different techniques in their own use-case. The solution to the use-case will be achieved by weighing the pros and cons of possible solutions and making the right design choices. These design choices are showcased in a presentation.
The student will build a product that consists of multiple procedural generation methodologies (noise, scatter, parametric etc). The specific product can be a scene that is procedurally generated or a tool that can be used to create new procedural created assets (city builder etc.). The assessment product will be a showreel video of the product suitable for the professional portfolio.
The entry requirement for this elective is that the student has passed level 1 of the elective.

/nl/course/2026/GTVB24ELRO2.outcomes: For this elective, level 2 students have to write 5 personal learning outcomes that adapt to their level, development needs and the CMGT LOLs. The learning outcomes have to be approved by the lecturer of the course.
/nl/course/2026/GTVB24ELRO2.content:
The Robotics elective is designed to provide students with an opportunity to explore the world of robotics and its applications. Through guided project work, students collaborate in teams to build robots that can express different emotions and interactions with users. Throughout the elective, students not only gain a solid foundation in the basics of electronics, Arduino programming, basic sensors, and automation in both software and hardware design but also in social interactions, empathy and how emotions can be detected and shown.
The first few weeks of the course focus on fundamental electronics and Arduino programming, while the latter weeks explore more advanced topics such as social interaction, empathy, and behaviour. Students are encouraged to take on specialized roles within their teams, while still learning the basics of electronics, power systems, basic sensors, Arduino programming, visual detection, and more.
Assessment of each student’s progress and understanding is based on a group report that describes the build process and outlines how each group member contributed to the final product. In addition, each student participates in an individual interview to assess their intrinsic understanding of the fundamental topics covered in the course. The minimum requirement for each student is to design and implement a functional contribution to the robot in each of the following areas: electronics, Arduino coding, and mechanical design/construction and how these can show and influence the state of the robot.
By the end of the course, students should be able to apply their newly acquired skills and knowledge to create a functional robot that can express different emotions and interact with users. Students who wish to pursue more advanced topics in robotics can continue their studies in machine learning, advanced AI, more advanced sensor systems, or industry-standard development platforms. The Robotics elective offers an exciting opportunity for students to develop their creativity, problem-solving skills, and critical thinking abilities, all while having fun building robots.
The entry requirement for this elective is that the student has passed level 1 of the elective.

/nl/course/2026/GTVB24ELRP2.outcomes:
Learning Outcomes
For this elective level 2 students have to write 5 personal learning outcomes that adapt to their level, development needs and the CMGT LOLs. The learning outcomes have to be approved by the lecturer of the course.
/nl/course/2026/GTVB24ELRP2.content:
To test (parts of) a game, you need people to experience your ideas. In the Rapid Prototyping elective you will build the skills and confidence to quickly develop representative, playable prototypes. Prototypes that you can use to test out your ideas.
The best way to learn is to do, so you will be creating prototypes based on provided themes and from any perspective you want, be it artist, designer or programmer. For each prototype you have two weeks, so imagine the joy and excitement of a Game Jam but feeling less groggy!
The course is set up as such that there is a lot of opportunity to generate ideas and for feedback on what you have created. At the end, you pick your best of three prototypes and iterate upon it adding an additional, provided theme.
The entry requirement for this elective is that the student has passed level 1 of the elective.

Upon approval of these prerequisites, students will work in a community of practitioners to develop a prototyped deliverable showcasing a narrative design topic. /nl/course/2026/GTVB23INT.outcomes:
Learning Outcomes
In a development portfolio, you must collect evidence and reflect on competences E, F, and G (these are mandatory) and one to your liking (one of A, B, C, or D). Per competency you choose one learning outcome to concentrate on.
Startup Route:
In the Startup Route students can do their internship in their own (startup) company. Due to the importance of competency A for starting or growing a business, competences A, E, F and G are mandatory in the Startup Route CMGT.
/nl/course/2026/GTVB23INT.content:
The internship is an external learning situation in which you work on the CMGT competencies.
During a period of 20 calendar weeks, you will work at a company of your choice, provided you work with professionals with CMGT related skills you can learn from. During that time, your schedule mirrors that of a company employee. This means that you follow the same daily hours as the company you work at, observe the same company rules, enjoy the same holidays, and exhibit the same professional behavior. It is a challenging but often rewarding period where you will discover much about both the field and your professional self.
The internship has three main goals:
You can apply the theory, knowledge and skills learned in programme to professional practices in the real world.
You understand the tension between theoretical concepts and practical applications outside of the CMGT classrooms.
You observe, reflect and learn about yourself as a future professional.
To reflect this, credits are not awarded for merely experiencing the outside world and fulfilling your job, but for the learning that takes place in this period. This is why you will create a development portfolio in which you will not only collect evidence of CMGT-related activities (like for example concepting, designing, developing, programming, or testing) but mostly will reflect on these activities to display your learning process.
Students can follow the CMGT Startup Route and do an internship in their own (startup) company.

/nl/course/2026/GTVB24IWP.outcomes:
LOL A Level 2 - The student acts and performs within a team, valuing the team's diversity and participates actively in the organisation of the project.
LOL B Level 2 - The student considers contextual factor in the analysis of a complex but structured problem.
LOL C Level 2 - The student employs appropriate prototyping and concepting methods to develop digital interactive prototypes.
LOL D Level 2 - The student can construct and iterate on solutions informed by relevant knowledge and theories.
LOL E Level 2 - The student can differentiate between different design decisions and explain how their choices address the design challenge.
LOL F Level 2 - The student knows their own strengths and weaknesses, can
formulate complex learning goals, reflects on and takes responsibility for managing their own learning process.
/nl/course/2026/GTVB24IWP.content:
Introduction
The IWP (Innovation workplace project) is a project that focuses on bringing students together one last time before graduation, to work on an open challenge related to games, play, playful design, or new technology.  The student will answer a question, opportunity, and/or design challenge in the context of innovation, interactivity, and technology. The project implies a design-oriented research cycle using the double diamond model and the foundation will be formed by input from the client, researchers, target audience, coaches, and experts. The aim is to involve the stakeholders, work within a team, and be open to getting to know new contexts and domains while exploring and learning to understand other roles and interests.
In addition, students need to look and find a client for their graduation project and timely prepare everything that is needed. A graduation boot camp will be held during week 6.
What to expect?
Experiment, explore, conceptualize, prototype, and evaluate coming up with a product/solution while developing a professional, inquisitive, and enterprising attitude!
Deal with an open challenge related to games, play, playful design, or new technology in the context of innovation, interactivity, and technology.
Be ready to explore and immerse in a new or unknown context!
Work with a client, a coach, and a team assigned to you.
Cocreate and involve others: students, researchers, clients, stakeholders, experts, and users.
Professionalism. Communication, planning, deliverables, etc. You are in charge, define priorities and timely communicate to the company and stakeholders in every part of the process.
Orientation and preparation for the graduation assignment.
Shaping the future. Many possibilities could unfold from the student–company relationship, including becoming partners of the company/client.
Use the double diamond model to plan and deliver.
The deliverables are not set by us, are set up by you based on the above.
Freedom to make this project your own process, take your own decisions and assume responsibility.
Discover, explore, and of course have fun again while coming up with a solution/prototype.
The assignment will be delivered in the form of a development portfolio.
The journey
To start defining the professional world you need to start being part of that world; work with clients, involve stakeholders, and prepare for graduation. The IWP focus is to prepare you in this journey, being a project focused on explore, cocreate and deliver, while being a preparation for the graduation assignment.
How?
Teamwork
Planning
Using the double diamond model
Coaching sessions
Cocreation
Showing progress and professionalism
Finding a client for your graduation project and submitting the documentation needed (Block 1, Week 6)
Delivering a Portfolio
Define your path!
Year 4 is about defining your professional world. The IWP is an opportunity to start doing it, defining your journey means using everything you have learned! This time, you are in charge, you need to work on that proposal considering the double diamond model, the goal of the project, time frame, etc. What research do you need? When will you deliver the first prototype? Testing? Iterations? Delivery? Value capturing? Roadmap? And for sure, more questions will come depending on the project.

/nl/course/2026/GTVB24GRA.outcomes:
LOL A: Organising and Managing. The CMGT professional is able to plan, manage and communicate process-based projects as part of a team.
LOL B: Contextualising and Framing. The CMGT professional is able to research the boundaries, scope, and requirements of a problem prior to exploring solutions.
LOL C: Exploring and Ideating. The CMGT professional is able to experiment with digital tools and ideate possible solution directions, in order to address a problem statement or design brief.
LOL D: Executing and Implementing. The CMGT professional is able to construct appropriate solutions, using relevant methodologies.
LOL E: Futures Innovating. The CMGT professional can deliver solutions that account for wider social ramifications, the needs of the client the requirements from research, taking ethical and intercultural values into account.
LOL F: Self-Fashioning. The CMGT professional builds connections, manages their own development, formulates learning goals, takes responsibility for their own learning process, and how they relate to the world.
/nl/course/2026/GTVB24GRA.content:
The final graduation capstone is a test of the junior professional's competences, demonstrating the student's ability to independently and meaningfully contribute to the resolution of a concrete problem in the area of creative media and game technologies. The graduation project is the last major test prior to graduation, functioning as the capstone of the CMGT programme.
The graduating student works full time for one semester (20 weeks) on a complex assignment in a professional situation within the CMGT domain, following a method and producing a final product demonstrating that the graduating student has attained all competencies of the CMGT programme.
During graduation, the student displays all parts of the T-shaped professional – the breadth of their learning and skills; how they apply this to a wider context; the depth of their own specialisation and learning path, and how tey have reached the end-level of all the CMGT competences.
The graduation capstone is assessed by a submitted portfolio and a final product, both assessed at a Final Demonstration. Both the portfolio and the product must be submitted prior to the Final Demonstration. By successfully completing the graduation capstone, the student demonstrates that they are ready to enter the working field in their capacity as a junior professional.
Admission to the graduation capstone is determined by the requirements listed in the CMGT Teaching and Assessment Regulations (TER), and upon approval of the graduation assignment by the CMGT Graduation Committee. Students will be coached in the search for their graduation assignment at the beginning of Year 4, during the Graduation Bootcamp (during period 1). During the graduation, students will participate in a Community of Learners with up to six other students, all of whom have been assigned the same graduation supervisor.

Je bent in staat om op aanwijzing van docenten/makers betekenis te geven aan creatieve processen en performing arts producten.
Ambachtelijk vermogen:
Je past instrumentele basisvaardigheden en basiskennis op aanwijzing van docenten/makers toe binnen de opeidingscontext.

Je bevraagt en reflecteert op de beroepspraktijk.
/nl/course/2026/LNVA26DA9.content:
Dansdomein
: in dit domein staat de beheersing van de danstechnische domeinonderdelen centraal. Het domein Danstechniek is verdeeld in een kern- en een basisdeel, waarbij de technische beheersing wordt verkregen in het basisdeel en in het kerndeel een brug wordt geslagen tussen de techniek, de verschillende dansstijlen en het werkveld.
Basis
Ballet
Ballet is de basis waarop alle andere danstechnieken voortbouwen.
Dit omvat ook het onderdeel Spitzen.
Moderne Dans
Moderne Dans dient als basis voor Poptheatermusicaldans-techniek, maar is ook een zelfstandige danstechniek. Moderne dans wordt gecombineerd met creatieve ontwikkeling. Creatieve ontwikkeling heeft als doel de student te leren creatieve producten te ontwikkelen, waaronder het ontwerpen van choreografieën.
Jazz Dans
Jazz Dans dient als basis voor Poptheatermusicaldans, maar is ook een zelfstandige danstechniek.
Acrodance
Acrodance helpt bij het optimaliseren van de fysieke ontwikkeling en de acrobatische vaardigheden. Acrodance is ondersteunend aan verschillende danstechnieken.
Trainingslessen
Trainingslessen worden aangeboden in periode E tijdens de repetities voor Project Integratie. In de trainingslessen worden de basistechnieken onderhouden.
Dansanalyse
Dansanalyse is gekoppeld aan de basisvakken in het Dansdomein. Dansanalyse omvat de theorie en de ontleding van de technieken.
Kern
Dans Trends
Hiphop is een zelfstandige danstechniek gebaseerd op niet-academische dansvormen. Dit domeinonderdeel is voortdurend aan vernieuwingen, trends en verandering onderhevig.
PopTheaterMusicalDans
In dit domeinonderdeel komen de verschillende dansstijlen bij elkaar en wordt een brug geslagen tussen de verschillende technieken. Ook leert de student creatieve producten te ontwikkelen waaronder het ontwerpen van choreografieën.
Theatre Latin Standard Dance
Theatre Latin Standard Dance is een onderdeel van het ballroomdansen en een verzamelnaam voor verschillende dansen die zijn ontstaan uit traditionele niet-academische dansvormen. Deze dansvormen zijn vanaf het begin van de 20ste eeuw gestandaardiseerd tot zelfstandige danstechnieken.
Tapdans
Tapdans dient als basis voor de Muziektheatertechniek en Danstechniek, maar is ook een zelfstandige techniek. Tapdans in een dansvorm waarbij men met de voeten ritmische klanken produceert.

Basis
Stemcoaching
Stemcoaching fungeert als ondersteuning voor de domeinonderdelen Acteren, Ensemblezang, Musical Theatre en Zangtechniek.

Zangtechniek dient als basis voor alle domeinonderdelen waarin zang voorkomt, maar is ook een zelfstandige techniek.
Kern

Acteren dient als basis voor het domeinonderdeel Musical Theatre, maar is in de vorm van musical Acteren ook een zelfstandig domeinonderdeel.

In Musical Theatre vormen de bestaande musicals, en dan in het bijzonder de dans- en ensemblezangstukken, het les- en leermateriaal. Musical Theatre is het kerndomeinonderdeel van het domein Muziektheater.

Zanginterpretatie is een apart onderdeel van Zangtechniek, waarbij de tekstinterpretatie centraal staat.

de praktijk- en theoriedomeinonderdelen van dit domein hebben als doel de student de mogelijkheid te geven om een persoonlijke leerroute vorm te geven. In de Intensive Weeks kunnen studenten deze route zelf vormgeven door middel van keuzepakketten
In trede 9Ad kan een student binnen dit domein onderdelen uit de opleiding Hbo- Bachelor Docent Dans volgen zodat de student kennismaakt met de praktijk van het lesgeven.

Kennisdomein
: in dit domein wordt kennis van de theoretische en historische achtergrond van de (podium)kunst verworven.
Basis
Personal Development (PD)
In PD wordt de student begeleid, in samenwerking met andere studenten of individueel, in zijn studieloopbaan, tijdens projecten en uitwisselingsprogramma’s.
Mens- en Bewegingskunde
uitsluitend in trede 9Ad
Mens- en Bewegingskunde omvat een basale kennis van anatomie, fysiologie en pathologie van het bewegings- en stemapparaat en vakspecifieke EHBO-vaardigheden.
Musicalgeschiedenis
Musicalgeschiedenis plaatst de musical in historisch perspectief.
Muziek Theorie
Muziek theorie gaat in op de theoretische aspecten van Muziek en omvat het kunnen lezen van tonen en intervallen.
Solfège
Solfège omvat het op het gehoor leren onderscheiden en het kunnen lezen van tonen en intervallen en wordt in verschillende modules gegeven, waarbij studenten eerst in trede 9Ad module één moeten hebben behaald om door te kunnen stromen naar module twee enz. In totaal zijn er vier modules die behaald moeten worden.
Kern
Theatertheorie
Theatertheorie plaatst de theorie van dans, beeldende kunst, musical, dramaturgie (de leer van de dramatische kunst) en muziek in (historisch) perspectief en legt hiermee de basis voor kennis over de ontwikkelingen in het hedendaagse culturele landschap. Studenten leren artistiek onderzoek doen binnen en tussen deze disciplines.
Onderzoek Paper AD
De student leert onderzoek doen onder begeleiding van de docent Onderzoek Paper AD.

Integratiedomein
: in dit domein maken de studenten kennis met hun toekomstige werkveld. Studenten doen praktijkervaring op door middel van podiumpraktijkstages en domein-overstijgende projecten op een niveau dat past bij de studiefase waarin de student zich bevindt.
Performing Knowledge/IWP
Binnen dit domeinonderdeel worden onder andere de theorie en de geschiedenis van het muziektheater in de praktijk gebracht. Hierbij ligt het accent op verbindingen leggen tussen Onderwijs, Onderzoek en Werkveld; Innovatiewerkplaats (IWP). In Performing Knowledge integreren studenten theorie door middel van onderzoek met de praktijk en brengen dit tot een innovatief geheel.
Projecten
ArtCore
: Binnen het Project ArtCore maken de studenten aan de hand van een thema samen met hun coach een presentatie c.q. Performing Arts-project om ervaring op te doen in ondernemen en creëren.
Project ADEP
: Het Project ADEP is een eindexamenonderdeel gekoppeld aan Project ArtCore.
Project “I”
:
Het Project “I” vindt vroeg in trede 9Ad plaats en heeft een oriënterende en samenwerkende doelstelling.
Project Integratie
: Bij het Project Integratie wordt onder leiding van diverse choreografen en regisseurs een theaterproduct uitgevoerd, waarbij verschillende domeinen geïntegreerd zijn tot een samenhangend geheel.
Theater Praktijkstages
Theater Praktijkstages bieden mogelijkheden om als uitvoerend kunstenaar, deels zelfstandig, deels onder supervisie, podium- en werkveldervaring op te doen.
I
nstituutsrepertoire
Bij domeinonderdeel Repertoire, wordt het Repertoire van LMIPA of uit het
Performing Arts
werkveld ingestudeerd en gerepeteerd.
