/nl/course/2026/BPVM26RIB1C.outcomes:
Students:
1. Define a theoretically grounded research problem on a selected topic.
2. Develop and justify research question(s).
3. Conduct critical and analytical literature review, synthesising and evaluating academic sources from multiple business disciplines.
4. Evaluate and select appropriate research designs and rigorous methods aligned with the research question(s).
5. Structure and develop a full academic research proposal using appropriate academic language and scholarly conventions.
Contribution to Programme Learning Outcomes (PLOs):
CLO1 contributes to PLO1 Research
CLO2 contributes to PLO1 Research
CLO3 contributes to PLO1 Research and PLO3 Interdisciplinary Approach
CLO4 contributes to PLO1 Research
CLO5 contributes to PLO5 Communication
/nl/course/2026/BPVM26RIB1C.content:
Strategic Focus Areas:
Entrepreneurship, Global Mindset and Sustainability
To conduct rigorous applied research, a strong theoretical and methodological foundation is required, supported by critical engagement with academic literature. The course Research in Business (RIB) develops students’ ability to conduct applied research in an interdisciplinary context, through systematic analysis of scholarly articles and methodological reasoning. The course is the first component of the curriculum of the IBP master program. Students learn to use academic literature, build arguments, and engage with different research methods. The course places particular emphasis on the intervention cycle.
The outcome of the course is a full research proposal demonstrating students’ ability to design a rigorous research study based on sound methodological principles. This proposal forms the foundation for the Innovation Assignment (INA) in the first semester and supports students’ research preparation for the master’s thesis in the second semester.
This course contributes to SDGs 4, 8, 9, 11, 12, 16 and 17.

/nl/course/2026/BPVM26INA1.outcomes:
Students:
1. Analyse a complex organisational or societal challenge using relevant data, research insights, and appropriate analytical tools to define a clear problem or opportunity.
2. Integrate perspectives, theories, and methods from multiple business disciplines to develop coherent insights and solution directions.
3. Design an innovative and sustainable solution that creates organisational and/or societal value, taking into account feasibility, risks, and stakeholder needs.
4. Work effectively in an interdisciplinary team and engage professionally with internal and external stakeholders throughout the project process.
5. Define and justify relevant impact indicators (economic, social, and environmental) to evaluate the proposed solution.
6. Communicate, critically reflect on, and defend the project approach, supporting evidence, proposed solution, and intended impact in a professional academic format.
CLO1 contributes to PLO1: Research
CLO2 contributes to PLO3: Interdisciplinary Approach
CLO3 contributes to PLO2: Innovation & Entrepreneurship
CLO4 contributes to PLO4: Professional Development & Leadership
CLO5 contributes to PLO1: Research and PLO2: Innovation & Entrepreneurship
CLO6 contributes to PLO4: Professional Development & Leadership and PLO5: Communication
/nl/course/2026/BPVM26INA1.content:
Strategic Focus Areas:
Entrepreneurship, Global Mindset and Sustainability
The Innovation Assignment (INA) is a course in which students work in interdisciplinary teams on real-life complex challenges sourced from professional practice or research partners. Students apply and extend their research knowledge and skills acquired in Research in Business, integrating theory and practice to develop an evidence-based, innovative solution.
The course begins with a networking event where students engage with external stakeholders to acquire a project assignment. They then follow an applied innovation and research process structured around systems thinking, problem analysis, ideation, design thinking, stakeholder analysis, value creation, validation, and impact definition.
Students develop integrated solutions by combining disciplinary perspectives and collaborating across backgrounds, with emphasis on synthesising knowledge, analysing complexity, and creating coherent and actionable solutions with societal and/or organisational value.
The course culminates in a portfolio of assessed work, including a capstone research-based academic poster, pitch, and defense, in which students present and justify their research, approach, solution design, and impact.
This course contributes to SDGs 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, and 17.

/nl/course/2026/BPVM26BKS1.outcomes:
Students:
1. Compare and critically evaluate theories, models and concepts from different disciplines
2. Demonstrate knowledge of the central BOKS themes.
3. Analyse a complex case study from a business perspective, integrating relevant fields relevant within the BOKS.
4. Interpret and critically analyze choices made within a business case, demonstrating corresponding knowledge of the literature.
5. Draw conclusions and formulate recommendations on a business case, supported by corresponding knowledge of the literature.
CLO1 contributes to PLO3: Interdisciplinary Approach
CLO2 contributes to PLO3: Interdisciplinary Approach
CLO3 contributes to PLO2 & PLO 3: Innovation & Entrepreneurship & Interdisciplinary Approach
CLO4 contributes to PLO3 and PLO5: Interdisciplinary Approach & Communication
CLO5 contributes to PLO3: Innovation & Entrepreneurship & Interdisciplinary Approach
/nl/course/2026/BPVM26BKS1.content:
Strategic Focus Areas: Entrepeneurship, Global Mindset and Sustainability
Body of Knowledge and Skilss (BKS) is a course in which students build an interdisciplinary frame of reference that supports their work across the MIBP programme. The course is organized around the Body of Knowledge and Skills (BOKS), which is structured into six themes: Transition Management, Sustainability, New Business & ICT, Globalisation & Localisation, Innovation & Entrepreneurship, and Organisational Design & Change.
Through workshops, guest lectures, guided reading, and case-based discussions, students engage with key theories, models, and concepts within each theme. They learn to move from broader perspectives toward the more specific lenses needed for their Innovation Assignment and master's Thesis. A central focus is the ability to compare and critically evaluate alternative theories, models, and conceptualizations rather than simply reproduce them.
Students apply these skills to a business case, analyzing the situation from a business perspective while drawing on relevant fields within the BOKS. They interpret choices made within the case in relation to the relevant literature and develop evidence-based conclusions and recommendations.
The course concludes with an individual oral exam in which students demonstrate their command of the BOKS themes and their ability to reason across disciplines.
This course contributes to SDGs 4, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12 and 13

/nl/course/2026/BPVM26PSK1C.outcomes:
Students:
1. Identify biographical elements, core qualities and pitfalls related to his behaviour patterns to increase sensitivity.
2. Critically reflects on leadership styles to meet professional standards and learning in interdisciplinary team contexts.
3. Synthesize their behavioural patterns and personality profile to guide ongoing personal development.
4. Demonstrate proactive behaviour, willingness to take risks in learning, experiment with new behaviours, and show self-awareness, resilience, and responsibility.
5. Demonstrate ethical leadership in an inspiring and supporting manner.
6. Verbally defend and reflect on their written portfolio, demonstrating effective academic and professional communication skills.
CLO1 contributes to: PLO 4
CLO2 contributes to: PLO 4
CLO3 contributes to: PLO 4
CLO4 contributes to: PLO 4
CLO5 contributes to: PLO 4
CLO6 contributes to:  PLO 5
/nl/course/2026/BPVM26PSK1C.content:
Strategic Focus Areas: Entrepeneurship and Global Mindset.
In the Professional Skills Development & Leadership (PSKL) course, students develop their learning process towards becoming interdisciplinary business professionals.
This course focuses on continuous professional development through reflection on behaviour, values, personality, leadership style, diversity & inclusion, and conflict style in a social and professional context, leading to increased self-awareness of strengths and areas for development.
Based on this, students build their leadership toolkit and experiment with new behaviours in workshops and practice-based experiences, supported by feedback and reflection.
Progress and development are documented in a portfolio, which forms the basis for assessment through an interview in which students demonstrate achievement of the course learning outcomes and their development process.
This course links to SDG 4; 8 and 16

/nl/course/2026/BPVM26THE1C.outcomes:
Students:
1. Formulate and justify a complex organizational or societal problem by critically analyzing relevant academic literature, data, and contextual factors, resulting in a clearly defined research objective and questions.
2. Critically integrate theories, concepts, and methods from multiple business disciplines (and, where relevant, adjacent fields) to develop a coherent analytical framework for addressing the research problem.
3. Design and execute an appropriate research methodology, demonstrating methodological justification, data integrity, and appropriate analytical skills in generating valid and reliable findings.
4. Develop and critically evaluate evidence-based, innovative, and sustainable solutions or insights that create organizational and/or societal value, explicitly considering feasibility, risks, stakeholder implications, and their economic, societal, and environmental impact. Translate findings into actionable, contextually appropriate recommendations for practice.
5. Demonstrate ethical awareness, professional responsibility, and critical reflection throughout the research process, including responsible stakeholder engagement and data handling, and justification of methodological choices, limitations, and implications.
6. Communicate and defend the research process, findings, and recommendations effectively across multiple formats, adapting content, argumentation, and style to the purpose and audience of each output in academic and professional contexts.
CLO1 contributes to PLO1: Research
CLO2 contributes to PLO3: Interdisciplinary Approach
CLO3 contributes to PLO1: Research
CLO4 contributes to PLO2: Innovation & Entrepreneurship
CLO5 contributes to PLO4: Professional Development & Leadership
CLO6 contributes to PLO5: Communication
/nl/course/2026/BPVM26THE1C.content:
Strategic Focus Areas: Entrepeneurship, Global Mindset and Sustainability
The Master Thesis is the proof by which students demonstrate their ability to independently make a substantial contribution towards the solution of a complex problem in an interdisciplinary professional context. The thesis is written in the form of a Journal Article Style Thesis (JAST), meaning that students produce an academic paper in a journal article format. As Business Professional with an MSc title, students are able to conceive innovative solutions that are relevant for the profession and based on relevant academic insights.
​
The thesis is a commissioner-driven, supervised learning process. To the extent possible, it simulates a professional work environment, emphasizing deadlines and professional standards for deliverables, as well as the need to make decisions and recommendations based on imperfect information. It recognizes the importance of being responsive to:
professional stakeholders, interested in the solution;
academic advances and standards in the relevant field;
the interdisciplinary environment, which requires effective cooperation with others.
This course enables students to address one or more Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) through student defined, impact oriented research.

/nl/course/2026/BPDM26OZ1.outcomes:
LU1: De deelnemer analyseert en definieert een reëel, complex praktijkprobleem en formuleert op basis daarvan een doelstelling, vraagstelling en deelvragen.
LU2: De deelnemer analyseert en synthetiseert relevante wetenschappelijke en praktijkgerichte literatuur en gebruikt deze kritisch om het praktijkprobleem, de begrippen en de deelvragen theoretisch te onderbouwen.
LU3: De deelnemer ontwerpt een passend en onderbouwd onderzoekstechnisch ontwerp voor beschrijvend en verklarend diagnostisch onderzoek, waarbij de methodologische keuzes, dataverzameling en analyse aansluiten bij de deelvragen.
LU4: De deelnemer past kennis, theorieën, modellen en methoden uit meerdere disciplines geïntegreerd toe bij het analyseren en verklaren van een reëel, complex praktijkprobleem
LU5: De deelnemer verzamelt, analyseert en interpreteert onderzoekgegevens systematisch en kritisch en creëert daarmee onderbouwde kennis over de aard, oorzaken en/of samenhang van het praktijkprobleem.
LU6: De deelnemer formuleert op basis van de onderzoeksresultaten onderbouwde conclusies een aanbevelingen, c.q. passende oplossingsrichtingen voor het reële, complexe praktijkprobleem en verantwoordt daarbij de gemaakte keuzes.
LU7: De deelnemer evalueert, bespreekt en verdedigt het onderzoeksproces, de methodologische en theoretische uitgangspunten en de onderzoeksresultaten kritisch, en reflecteert op de kwaliteit, de beperkingen en bruikbaarheid van het onderzoek.
/nl/course/2026/BPDM26OZ1.content:
Binnen de opleiding gaan deelnemers werken aan complexe vraagstukken in de eigen beroepspraktijk. Deze complexe vraagstukken hebben daarmee een interdisciplinair karakter en worden gekenmerkt door een diversiteit aan verschillende belanghebbenden met verschillende belangen. Het oplossen van deze complexe problemen vereist empirische onderbouwing. Praktijkgericht, toegepast onderzoek is daarom noodzakelijk. Praktijkgericht, toegepast onderzoek volgt de regulatieve cyclus (diagnose, ontwerp, verandering, evaluatie) en heeft als doel een directe bijdrage te leveren aan de beroepspraktijk door oplossingen aan te dragen voor praktijkproblemen.
In de module OZ1 staat het onderzoeken van een praktijkvraagstuk uit de eigen beroepscontext centraal. Deelnemers formuleren een onderzoeksvoorstel en voeren vervolgens een verklarend, diagnostisch onderzoek uit. Het doel is om een complex organisatievraagstuk systematisch te analyseren, onderliggende oorzaken bloot te leggen en een goed onderbouwde probleemdefinitie te ontwikkelen.

/nl/course/2026/BPDM26BOKS1.outcomes:
LU1 – Verklaren en verbinden: De deelnemer verklaart en verbindt theorieën, modellen en concepten uit verschillende wetenschappelijke basisdisciplines, functionele bedrijfskundige disciplines en relevante stakeholderperspectieven ten behoeve van de analyse van complexe organisatievraagstukken.
LU2 – Analyseren: De deelnemer analyseert complexe organisatievraagstukken vanuit een integraal bedrijfskundig perspectief met behulp van relevante theorieën, modellen en concepten uit verschillende wetenschappelijke basisdisciplines en functionele bedrijfskundige disciplines en houdt daarbij rekening met relevante interne en externe stakeholderperspectieven.
LU3 – beoordelen en beargumenteren: De deelnemer beoordeelt en beargumenteert keuzes, conclusies en handelingsperspectieven in een organisatievraagstuk op basis van relevante wetenschappelijke literatuur, verschillende disciplinaire perspectieven, stakeholderbelangen en een systematische analyse.
LU4 – Academisch kritisch positioneren: De deelnemer construeert een korte kritische literatuurstudie waarin relevante wetenschappelijke standpunten worden samengevat, met elkaar worden vergeleken en kritisch worden beoordeeld, resulterend in een eigen, onderbouwde academische positionering.
/nl/course/2026/BPDM26BOKS1.content:
BOKS biedt deelnemers de theoretische en conceptuele kennis die nodig is om complexe bedrijfskundige vraagstukken te analyseren, te beoordelen en van onderbouwde adviezen en oplossingen te voorzien.
BOKS is nadrukkelijk interdisciplinair van karakter. Vanuit verschillende perspectieven wordt gekeken naar organisaties, hun omgeving en de ontwikkeling die daarop van invloed is. Daarbij komen onder andere transitiekunde, systeemkunde, integrale bedrijfskunde, duurzaamheid, digitale transformatie, lokalisatie en globalisatie, innovatie & ondernemerschap aan bod.

/nl/course/2026/LBVP26DID1C.outcomes:
PLO1: International Business Opportunities
In this course, PLO1 is supported through Learning Line 1 by strengthening students’ capacity to work with evidence in international business contexts. Students develop skills to analyse and interpret data to inform managerial judgment. This enables them to identify and evaluate international business opportunities more effectively.
Specifically, in this course, students are expected to develop the following competencies:
Learning Line: Research & Data Analytics
CLO 1: Apply critical thinking and evidence-based reasoning to evaluate data, generate insights, and propose justified business decisions.
CLO 2: Conduct data analysis using digital tools to collect, interpret, and visualise information that supports informed and actionable managerial judgment.
PLO2: Business Transformation
This course positions students to engage with business transformation in a global and digitally mediated context. Learning Line 2 operationalises this focus by strengthening evidence-based business communication and professional development. It does so through structured quantitative reporting and the responsible use of digital and AI tools to support data-informed decisions.
Specifically, in this course, students are expected to develop the following competencies:
Learning Line: Global Mindset & Professional Development
CLO 1: Demonstrate digital and AI literacy to enhance the accuracy and ethical quality of data-informed decision-making.
PLO3: Relationship Management
In this course, students develop the ability to produce structured academic reports that present ideas in a coherent and logical manner, employ appropriate and precise professional language, incorporate source material effectively, and adhere to established academic conventions including formatting and accurate referencing.
Learning Line: Global Mindset & Professional Development
CLO 1: Produce a structured professional product that demonstrates quantitative and practical research skills in communicating data-driven business insights.
/nl/course/2026/LBVP26DID1C.content:
This course equips students with the analytical and digital competencies to make data-informed business decisions in international contexts. By integrating critical thinking, digital literacy, ethical AI use, and professional English, students learn to analyse and communicate data-driven insights that guide responsible managerial action.
Aligned with SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), the course prepares students to become future-oriented IB professionals who leverage digital and AI literacy to drive ethical, inclusive, and data-driven growth across international markets

/nl/course/2026/LBVP26BES1C.outcomes:
PLO1: International Business Opportunities
In this course, students work in groups to make business decisions within a simulated environment, starting with business strategy, adapting to market changes, and making critical decisions across key business areas.
Learning Line: Management
CLO1: The student can define clear business goals and strategies, ensuring consistency across decisions, such as pricing, quality, and market positioning, to achieve long-term organizational value.
PLO2: Business Transformation
In this course, students reflect on their results and adjust their business strategies or decisions as needed.
Learning Line: Management
CLO1: The student can reflect on the company's performance in the simulated environment and make data-driven adjustments to their strategies, optimizing sustainable international business practices in future periods.
PLO3: Relationship Management
In this course, the students work in a culturally diverse group and together work as managers of their company in a simulated environment.
Learning line: Global mindset and professional development
CLO1: The student can effectively summarize the entire teamwork process.
CLO2: The student can communicate (business) messages effectively and persuasively using advanced English to an (un)informed audience.
PLO4: Self-Management
In this course, the students increase self-awareness during their project work in a group.
Learning Line: Global mindset and professional development
CLO1: The student can identify their own strengths, weaknesses, and cultural foundations to increase self-awareness.
CLO2: The student can understand their role in a project team, give and receive feedback to improve cooperation.
/nl/course/2026/LBVP26BES1C.content: This course introduces key business domains—marketing, accounting, and supply chain management—in a global context to build students’ understanding of decision-making within a business simulation. Personal and intercultural development sessions support the group's work process, while a business communication workshop equips students to effectively present their combined insights. Together, these elements foster responsible entrepreneurship and strategic thinking aligned with SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth.

/nl/course/2026/LBVP26OCB1A.outcomes:
PLO1: International Business Opportunities
In this course, students develop core competencies in Organisational Behaviour (OB) and Consumer Behaviour (CB) so students can translate organisational insight and market understanding into actionable international strategies.
Learning Line 1:
Management
CLO1
: Understand how individuals and groups behave inside organisations.
Learning Line 2:
Marketing
CLO2
: Understand how consumers perceive, decide, and act in markets.
PLO2: Business Transformation
In this course, students connect foundational theory to practical transformation mechanisms, including motivation, change management, and engagement, so they can diagnose current states and design evidence-based interventions.
Learning Line 1:
Management + Marketing
CLO1
: Explain core OB/CB theories of motivation and change management in international organisational settings.
Learning Line 2:
Management + Marketing
CLO2
: Understand theoretical concepts in improving employee and consumer engagement.
/nl/course/2026/LBVP26OCB1A.content: This course introduces core concepts of OB and CB. Students learn how individuals and groups behave within organisations and how consumers perceive and act in global markets. Integrating cross-cultural perspectives, the course develops students’ global mindset and analytical skills to understand motivation, decision-making, and change in international contexts. By linking behavioural insights to responsible management, OCB1 contributes to SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), fostering sustainable organisational practices and consumer engagement strategies in an interconnected world.

/nl/course/2026/LBVP26GTM1C.outcomes:
PLO1: International Business Opportunities
This course equips students with talent-management competencies that enable firms to identify and act on international business opportunities. Specifically, students will build HR and intercultural capabilities that support evidence-based people decisions across borders.
In this course, students are expected to develop the following competencies in the field of talent management:
Learning Line 1:
Management
CLO1
: Students can develop an understanding of Human Resource (HR) processes in international contexts.
Learning Line 2:
Management + Global Mindset & Professional Development
CLO2
: Students can demonstrate knowledge and skills in the areas of cultural management and business communication, contributing to HR-related decisions.
PLO2: Business Transformation
This course focuses on talent management as a key factor of sustainable organisational change. Accordingly, students will build competencies that translate transformation principles into practice through the following learning lines and module learning outcomes:
Learning Line 1:
Management
CLO1
: Students can put theory into practice and produce an actionable talent management plan for a fictional or actual company.​
Learning Line 2:
Management + Global Mindset & Professional Development
CLO2
: Students can demonstrate the ability to manage the impact of culture on HR-related decisions.
/nl/course/2026/LBVP26GTM1C.content:
This course explores talent management in international business contexts, emphasising how organisations attract, develop, and retain talent across cultures to drive sustainable growth.
Students develop a global mindset through analysing HR processes, ensuring diversity and inclusion, integrating intercultural awareness, and creating strategic workforce planning in multinational settings.
By translating theory into actionable talent management plans, the course aligns with SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), cultivating responsible, inclusive, and sustainable people practices in global organisations.

/nl/course/2026/LBVP26MFA1A.outcomes:
PLO1: International Business Opportunities
In this course, the student develops basic knowledge and skills in financial and managerial accounting to understand how organizations create and communicate value to both internal and external stakeholders.
Leaning Line: Economic, Finance & Accounting:
